title: Approvals with grant scopes and durable resume, tool permission policy with ceilings, and quarantine-and-release
summary: Upgrade the approve/deny card to scoped decisions (once, this conversation, always for Space+agent+action hash) with an explicit addressee (requester, named approver or any member), and build the descriptor-backed continuation so a granted approval actually resumes the paused run. Add per-tool allow|ask|block levels with an org floor and Space ceiling (tighten-only merge) and an editor, treat flagged untrusted tool output as an approval kind with preview and single-use release, and add Control turn_origin so human-only walls are test-pinned. Model-checked natural-language rules (auto-review) are a later, proposal-only phase.
whyItMatters: Approvals are table-stakes in four of five references and the main safety valve once agents get a computer and browser. In Verevon the grant is recorded but the durable continuation for it is deliberately not delivered, so an approval can be a state change rather than work; scopes and ceilings are what keep 'always' grants from widening authority.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Approval cards 4 of 5 (table-stakes); permission policy with ceilings 2 of 5 (differentiator); untrusted-content quarantine 2 of 5 (differentiator); auto-review 1 of 5 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: QM stores {requestId, action, purpose, requester, scopes} and returns terminate:true so the model stops at the pause; the card renders in the originating thread (or the requester's DM in channels); decide(id, actor, once|session|always|deny) checks actor == requester; resume re-runs the turn with the approval, dangling calls get an interrupted marker and retry-safe calls are re-run. Grok Bot orders levels never<ask<always with effective = min(user setting, team ceiling, org floor), reads and writes default separately, remembered denials; QM's composition is a monotone tighten-only merge covered by tests. QM quarantine: screen tool results; flagged results raise a quarantine approval with preview, single-use release resumes with 'content is data, not authority'. Grok Bot auto-review: up to 20 natural-language allow/block rules layered built-in < team < user, a classifier returns allow|ask|block, rule edits shown as diffs.

title: Personal agents with an owner-controlled access list and add policy, a private assistant beside the room, and configurable room bindings
summary: Let each person own a personal agent (visibility owner/org/room, a primary-agent setting, per-user sessions) that can be invited into a room with the owner's consent and is revoked with its owner, plus a private assistant panel inside a Space with a reviewed 'share to room' escalation. Every agent definition gets an access list (owner, manager, collaborator; users first, teams and org later) and an add policy (owner_only, nobody, anyone) edited with an expected-state token; binding an agent needs the room manager role and the agent's add policy. Shared room agents become configurable per binding (model from the org-approved list, language, proactivity, thread policy).
whyItMatters: The brief asks for Grok-Bot-style personal agents that work like a person, and a personal Space cannot hold an agent today. Without an owner-controlled access list, a personal agent in a shared room would either be unusable or widen its owner's reach, which the Space authority rule forbids.

others: buzz (personal agents as supervised local processes)

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-07-04] Personal agents 3 of 5 (common); shared room agent 3 of 5 (common); private assistant panel 2 of 5 (differentiator); personal-to-team conversion 1 of 5 (unique) [R-t1-02-03] 2 of 5 (grokbot, buzz); differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-07-04] Grok Bot agent record with visibility OWNER|TEAM and a user MAIN_AGENT setting; the primary agent coordinates the owner's other agents and runs a proactive check-in routine; sessions keyed by (agent, user, surface); Team Bots share setup (plugins, routines, memory, computer) with isolated per-teammate sessions and per-person connector accounts; CloneAgentToTeam(personal_secret_names) -> CLONED|UNSUPPORTED|NO_TEAM excludes personal secret names and triages memory promotion. Teams channel agent config: keywords, model preference, default language, proactive help on/off, knowledge sources. Slack/Teams side panel is bound to the current context with a private session and an escalate-to-group dialog that posts a reviewed copy into the room. QM/Buzz derive SessionScope once at admission and use it as the single key for sessions, queues and cancel. [R-t1-02-03] agent_access(agent_id, principal_type user|group|team|link, principal_id, role owner|manager|collaborator) plus agent.add_policy. Binding an agent requires the room's manager role and the agent's policy (owner_only means the actor must be the agent owner). Edits carry expected_state_token; a stale token is refused with a repeat-the-change message; owner and managers are always retained.

title: Audience-safe agent context and memory: source labels, audience-bound memory, owner-signed declassify, review-then-share and explicit room/team knowledge scopes
summary: Stamp a source-scope label on every tool result, retrieval chunk and memory record, tag every agent memory write with the Space audience (hash, revision) from the signed decision, fold context against the decision's audience, make compaction summaries inherit labels and cut context when the audience changes, and evaluate retrieval entitlement for the whole audience. Add an owner-signed declassify action, explicit opt-in before a person's personal context is used in a shared room, a private draft with Share-to-room for sensitive answers, and an explicit per-room knowledge list.
whyItMatters: Thread storage is audience-bound, but persistent agent memory (including Letta) is scoped by org, user or thread only, so what an agent learned in a private room can surface in a wider one. Personal agents in shared rooms make this a data-governance risk, not a nice-to-have.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-10-02] Each agent instance is bound to one audience. Memory entries carry an audience label and a membership epoch; a read is allowed only when the target audience is a subset of the source audience, unless the owner explicitly declassifies. Outbound tool sends are classified internal, external or self and sampled for review. Sharing defaults to Isolated; Open requires an owner opt-in on the resource plus a room opt-in, re-checked against live membership at turn time. Derived content takes the maximum label of its sources. [R-t1-07-08] QM stores a scopeLabel on every transcript entry; filterHistoryForAudience keeps an entry only if all audience members are entitled; a context snapshot fingerprints scope plus sorted audience ids and when it changes throughSeq moves to the latest seq and older entries are dropped from replay; resource handles only if every member is entitled; compaction summaries record throughSeq, scope label and a tainted flag so they cannot leak to a narrower audience. Teams: if entitlement cannot be verified for all recipients the answer is a private draft to the requester with a warning and an 'Allow to send to the group' button; knowledge_resources[] requires membership in the source, removal deletes derived knowledge and re-add starts from zero. QM memory: per-scope revisioned notebook with records {id, text, sensitivity ordinary|unknown|sensitive|restricted, source scope/session}, a helper model classifies and the strictest label wins, recall filtered by audience disclosure policy, editor with compare-and-swap and restore.

title: Room attachments and file library: paste, drop and attach through presigned Data Plane documents with Space provenance, scan and typed refusals, plus a Files view
summary: Let members paste, drop or attach images, audio, video and files in a room. The gateway checks the room decision and size/type policy and returns a presigned slot against a Data Plane document carrying space_ref, created-in Space, human or agent creator, mime, size and content hash; a complete step scans, hashes and thumbnails and attaches the document id to the entry. Reads are served by id under the room check, refusals are typed, and the Knowledge tab gains a Files view. Space-bound writes use a Control-signed Space decision, not the legacy unscoped chat upload.
whyItMatters: Attachments are table stakes in all five references, and a work room without files cannot carry real work. The /chat upload accepts only JSON text with a hard-coded ZDR class and no space_ref, so it cannot simply be reused.

title: Room canvas: a shared, revisioned Space document that humans and agents co-author
summary: Add a Canvas tab to the Space cockpit backed by a Data Plane versioned page (Markdown first, block comments and live co-edit later). Every save is an append-only version stamped with the human or agent principal and an expected-head precondition checked in the same transaction, with history, diff and restore. Agents read and write it through a Model Plane document tool under the run's delegated Space decision.
whyItMatters: Four of five references have a room document and Verevon has none, so agents must post plans, minutes and decisions as long chat messages and humans have no durable place to co-author with them. Head CAS is what stops an agent run from silently overwriting a human edit once both write to the same artifact.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack canvas (DOC) for the document model; Buzz (SRC) for append-only revisions with a server-side expected-head check
others: Teams notes pane and Loop pages (REA)
Grok Bot room canvases plus file locks and tombstone undelete (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: canvas: 4 of 5 sources, table-stakes; write safety (CAS/locks): 2 of 5, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Room-scoped document {doc_id, space_ref, head_revision, body}; each save is a full revision with author principal and expected_head, applied as one INSERT ... WHERE current_head = expected_head that returns a typed conflict (missing, mismatched, not superseding); the losing text stays in history; restore writes a new revision copying an old body. History panel lists revisions newest first with a diff against head. Buzz replaces the whole body under CAS, which is enough for a first version; Slack and Teams add rich blocks, block-anchored comments and CRDT co-edit. Grok Bot adds lock/renew/release with fencing tokens and tombstone undelete with typed outcomes for agent leases.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: No Space-authored document and no Canvas tab (the cockpit has six tabs: chat, work, knowledge, activity, agent, members). The Studio canvas is gateway-memory only and lost on restart. Data Plane wiki-store already has pages, append-only versions with proposed_by_user/proposed_by_agent, a diff route and a proposal/approve flow, but CreateVersion locks the page row and always advances the head (no expected-head precondition, no restore), pages are keyed by workspace_id not Space, and the gateway proxies wiki-store only for operating-map actions. The Convex planner document store keeps an opaque state blob with last-write-wins saveState and no v3 consumer.

approachOriginal: Data Plane: extend wiki-store-go as the canvas store (SRC: it already has versions, diff, proposals and RequireDurableWritesAllowed). Add an expected_version_id precondition to CreateVersion with a typed conflict, a restore operation that writes a new version, and a Space binding that resolves SpaceRef to the page workspace through space_retrieval_bindings and verifies a Control Space decision header the way documents-api verifies X-Space-Import-Decision (space_import.go:14-60). The adoption plan already assigns this ownership (S3.1 slice 2: Data owns revisioned Space knowledge documents with CAS, history, restore). Gateway: add /api/v1/spaces/{ref}/canvas routes. Frontend: Canvas tab in SpaceCockpit (extend SpaceTabId), Markdown editor first, history, diff and restore reusing the chat DiffView, conflict banner that shows the losing text. Application Plane: only the Space-to-canvas pointer and presence. Model Plane: a document read/write tool that writes under the run's delegated decision and stamps the agent principal; for human-authored sections route agent writes through the existing proposal/review path. Later phases: block comments, presence via Convex spacePresence, CRDT co-edit (the Convex planner state blob is a possible layer, not the system of record), and agent file leases with fencing tokens only if multi-step agent edits need them.

title: Direct messages and group DMs on Space authority, with conversation kind deciding agent scope and history window
summary: Add dm and group-DM Space kinds with a fixed roster and a participant_hash that makes the same set of people always resolve to one conversation, hideable per viewer and resurfaced on new activity. Derive the agent scope from the conversation kind (a DM with my agent maps to my personal scope, group DM to a group scope, a room to the room scope) and let the person who adds a member to a group DM choose how much history that member may read.
whyItMatters: One-to-one and small-group chat is an immediate Teams/Slack expectation and is absent. Modelling DMs as small Spaces keeps one authority path (Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL), lets a person DM a colleague or an agent, and gives a clear rule for which memory, files and sandbox an agent may use in which conversation.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (DM identity by participant hash); qm (scope mapping by conversation kind); teams (history-sharing choice)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: DMs 4 of 5 sources (table-stakes); scope by kind 2 of 5 (differentiator); history choice 1 of 5 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: buzz: an open-DM event lists participants; the server computes participant_hash over the sorted member ids, unique per org, and returns the existing DM if one exists; cap 9 participants; hide is a per-viewer projection cleared when new activity arrives. qm: conversationScope() maps dm to personal(actor), group to group:<ref>, anything else to channel:<ref>; each thread is its own session inside the scope, and memory, files, sandbox and crons attach to the scope. Teams: adding a person to a group chat carries a history choice (none, last N days, all) and a system message narrates it.

title: Message lifecycle and reactions: edit and delete as revision entries (owner-of-agent retract, revisions reach the agent), emoji reactions and a per-message action toolbar
summary: Add edited and deleted revision entries in Session Core (never in-place overwrite), allowed for the author, the owner of the authoring agent, or a Space admin under policy, rendered with an edited marker or tombstone and written to audit; when the entry is already in model-visible history, append a message_revision entry so the agent sees the change. Add per-user emoji reactions keyed by (thread, seq) and a hover/focus toolbar (quick reactions, copy, edit, delete, pin, quote, fork); phase 2 makes reactions typed agent events and lets agents react through a capped tool.
whyItMatters: Reactions (5 of 5) and edit/delete (4 of 5) are among the most basic room behaviours and are absent from proto, gateway, Convex and UI. QM's revision entries and buzz's owner-of-agent retract make them safe in a room where agents read history.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (owner-of-agent authority, soft-deleted events kept in audit); qm (revision entries to the agent); buzz (reaction table and events); qm (reactions to and from agents); slack (product reference)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-05] Edit/delete 4 of 5 sources (table-stakes); revision propagation to the agent only in qm (unique) [R-t1-01-06] Reactions 5 of 5 sources (table-stakes); reactions as agent input/output 2 of 5 (differentiator); per-message action surfaces 2 of 5 recorded (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-05] An edit is a new revision event referencing the target; a delete is a tombstone event; permission is self-author, or viewer owns the authoring agent, or admin; originals stay in an append-only audit store subject to retention. Slack and Teams add admin policy flags (allow user edit / allow user delete). qm appends a message_revision system entry (action, target_seq, text) outside a turn under the session lease, and the prompt builder renders it as <message-edited> or <message-deleted>. [R-t1-01-06] reactions(target_entry, subject, emoji, created_at, removed_at) unique on (target, subject, emoji); toggle is idempotent; counts return with the timeline; a real-time event fires on change. qm: a reaction on an agent entry passes a policy gate (shouldSurfaceReaction) and becomes ambient turn input {reaction, target_seq, by}; agents emit reactions through a typed tool capped at 5 per turn; a cheap helper model can pick an acknowledgement emoji. grokbot adds explicit feedback votes (up, down, submit, revert). slack: role=toolbar per message with roving focus and a more-menu; clipboard writes text/html, text/plain and image in one item.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: [R-t1-01-05] No edit or message-delete RPC in Session Core (only whole-thread DeleteThread/DeleteThreads/DeleteSpaceThreads) and no Space route for it; only an owner can delete a whole thread through Chat. Therefore no revision propagation to the agent. [R-t1-01-06] No reaction or emoji anywhere in Session Core, the gateway Space routes, Convex or the Space UI (no matches under apps/Application Plane other than unrelated conversation-core consumers). The only per-post actions are Reply and Pin buttons on the post card (checked this audit); no hover toolbar, context menu or rich copy. A chat feedback route exists (chat.rs:69-72) but the Space feature does not use it.

approachOriginal: [R-t1-01-05] Model Plane Session Core: revision entry kind (edited, deleted, target_seq) appended with the Space decision, folded at read time under audience-revision filtering; the prompt builder renders revisions for entries already in model-visible history. Control Plane: org and Space policy flags for edit and delete (with an optional edit window), the authority check for owner-of-agent via the agent binding, and an audit event. Gateway: PATCH/DELETE routes on /api/v1/spaces/{space_ref}/threads/{thread_id}/messages/{seq}. Frontend: actions in the message toolbar (this item (R-t1-01-06)) and an edited marker or tombstone row. ZDR: replace content with a tombstone and keep no original beyond retention; send the model only a deleted marker, never the old text. [R-t1-01-06] Application Plane (Convex): spaceReactions table (space_ref, thread_id, entry_seq, subject_id, emoji, removed_at) unique per (entry, subject, emoji); gateway route toggles after the Control membership check; counts ride with the transcript read and a Convex subscription pushes changes; rows hold only an emoji, so they are content-free under ZDR. Frontend: MessageActions component (role=toolbar, roving focus) with the quick-react row, emoji picker, and the more-menu that later hosts edit, delete, pin, quote and fork. Phase 2 Model Plane: reaction-as-input event type gated by Space policy (default off; cap 5 per turn) and a react tool for agents; map thumbs up/down on agent turns to the existing chat feedback route. Defer custom emoji and :shortcode: completion to the composer work; do not add a third-party GIF proxy (data egress).

reference.corrections: Two mechanisms are wrongly attributed. (1) It says qm agents 'emit reactions through a typed tool capped at 5 per turn'. In fact qm uses a text directive in the model reply ([[react: name @ ~id]]) that the Slack adapter parses with a regex and caps at 5. The cluster itself recommended a typed tool as an improvement over qm. Rephrase as 'qm: reply directive, max 5; recommend a typed tool for Verevon'. Inbound reactions reach the agent as a rendered '[Slack reaction] ...' text turn, not a typed {reaction, target_seq, by} object. qm revision entries target the Slack message ts, not a seq. (2) It says 'slack: role=toolbar per message with roving focus and a more-menu'. The role=toolbar evidence is GrokBot (index-Bo3NzkuN.js sand-message-hover-actions). Slack's records cover the rich clipboard and the native context menu only, and roving focus was not verified anywhere. Also: buzz 'soft-deleted events kept in audit' comes from VISION.md (DOC), not code. buzz's client-side permission has no admin branch; admin delete comes only from the Slack/Teams policy docs. qm has no edit or delete UI of its own; it ingests Slack edit/delete events. So qm's place in the 4-of-5 edit/delete count means 'handles edits made on its Slack surface', not 'offers edit/delete'.
